title: Twenty Thousand Leagues under the Sea
author: Jules Verne

Four Thousand Leagues under the Pacific

From Cape Horn to the Amazon

waypoints.name: Fifth Avenue Hotel
waypoints.notes: Aronnax receives the invitation in New York; mapped to the historical Fifth Avenue Hotel area.

waypoints.name: Brooklyn pier
waypoints.notes: Departure point for the Abraham Lincoln.

waypoints.name: Tropic of Capricorn, 105 W
waypoints.notes: The Abraham Lincoln cuts the tropic of Capricorn at 105 degrees longitude.

waypoints.name: Equator, 110 W
waypoints.notes: The frigate crosses the equator on the 110th meridian.

waypoints.name: Japan encounter
waypoints.notes: Gutenberg text gives 31 deg 15 min N, 136 deg 42 min E, less than two hundred miles from Japan.

waypoints.name: Nautilus boarding
waypoints.notes: The castaways discover the Nautilus after the collision.

waypoints.name: Crespo Island
waypoints.notes: Gutenberg text gives 32 deg 40 min N, 157 deg 50 min W.

waypoints.name: Crespo submarine forest
waypoints.notes: The Nautilus is stranded in five fathoms for the undersea walk.

waypoints.name: Clermont-Tonnerre atoll
waypoints.notes: One of the Pomotou/Tuamotu atolls observed before Vanikoro.

waypoints.name: Tahiti
waypoints.notes: Seen to the east on 15 December.

waypoints.name: Aurou, New Hebrides
waypoints.notes: Mapped near Aore/Espiritu Santo for the New Hebrides passage.

waypoints.name: Vanikoro
waypoints.notes: The text gives Vanou harbor as 16 deg 4 min S, 164 deg 32 min E.

waypoints.name: Torres Strait reef
waypoints.notes: Grounding location in Torres Strait, near Gueboroar and the Papuan coast.

waypoints.name: Gueboroar Island
waypoints.notes: Mapped near the Torres Strait island visited while the Nautilus is grounded.

waypoints.name: Gueboroar inland grove
waypoints.notes: Estimated inland point for the chapter 20 hunting and gathering walk.

waypoints.name: Ceylon pearl bank
waypoints.notes: Mapped west of Mannar/Ceylon for Nemo's pearl-bank excursion.

waypoints.name: Red Sea, 21 deg 30 min N
waypoints.notes: The text gives 21 deg 30 min N before the Arabian Tunnel passage.

waypoints.name: Gulf of Pelusium
waypoints.notes: Mediterranean exit of Nemo's fictional Arabian Tunnel.

waypoints.name: Grecian Archipelago
waypoints.notes: Aegean shaping point near Santorini.

waypoints.name: Atlantis
waypoints.notes: The text gives 33 deg 22 min latitude and 16 deg 17 min longitude; longitude is modeled west in the Atlantic.

waypoints.name: Submarine coal lagoon
waypoints.notes: Fictional volcanic refuge for the Nautilus.

waypoints.name: Atlantic abyss
waypoints.notes: The Nautilus descends to 16,000 yards, or four leagues, in the Atlantic abyss.

waypoints.name: South Pole
waypoints.notes: Nemo's fictional open sea at the South Pole.

waypoints.name: Ice prison
waypoints.notes: Position inferred for the post-pole iceberg imprisonment.

waypoints.name: Poulp battle
waypoints.notes: Estimated North Atlantic/Antilles location for the giant-poulp attack.

waypoints.name: Atlantic cable
waypoints.notes: A shaping point for the transatlantic cable inspection.

waypoints.name: Avenger wreck
waypoints.notes: The text gives 47 deg 24 min latitude, 17 deg 28 min longitude for the wreck of the Avenger.

waypoints.name: Lofoten shore
waypoints.notes: Aronnax, Conseil, and Ned Land recover on the Norwegian coast.

paths.title: New York to Brooklyn pier
paths.notes: Aronnax and Conseil hurry from the hotel to the Abraham Lincoln at Brooklyn.

paths.title: Abraham Lincoln search cruise
paths.notes: The frigate leaves Brooklyn, rounds Cape Horn, crosses the tropic of Capricorn at 105 W and the equator on 110 W, then meets the Nautilus near Japan.

paths.title: Castaways on the Nautilus
paths.notes: Aronnax, Conseil, and Ned Land survive the collision and climb onto the unknown vessel.

paths.title: Black River to Crespo
paths.notes: The Nautilus follows the Kuro-Scivo; Crespo is described as about 1,800 miles from the starting point.

paths.title: Crespo sea-floor walk
paths.notes: Nemo leads a diving-suit hunt through the submarine forest while the Nautilus rests in five fathoms.

paths.title: Four thousand leagues under the Pacific
paths.notes: Distance is scaled to the chapter title's under-Pacific cumulative travel while the curve follows Pomotou, Tahiti, New Hebrides, and Vanikoro anchors.

sourceRefs.label: four thousand leagues under the Pacific

paths.title: Vanikoro to Torres Strait
paths.notes: The text gives 750 leagues from Vanikoro/La Perouse's group to the southeast point of Papua.

paths.title: Gueboroar landing
paths.notes: While the Nautilus is grounded, Aronnax, Conseil, and Ned Land row ashore and explore the island.

paths.title: Gueboroar island foray
paths.notes: Aronnax, Conseil, and Ned Land spend a few days ashore hunting and gathering while the Nautilus waits for the tide.

paths.title: Indian Ocean crossing
paths.notes: The Nautilus leaves the coral kingdom for the Indian Ocean, passes near Cocos, and approaches the pearl banks of Ceylon.

paths.title: Ceylon pearl dive
paths.notes: Nemo takes the party on foot across the pearl bank and saves an Indian diver from a shark.

paths.title: Ceylon to the Red Sea
paths.notes: The Nautilus crosses the Sea of Oman, passes Aden, and enters the Red Sea.

paths.title: Arabian Tunnel
paths.notes: Nemo's fictional submarine passage runs beneath Suez from the Red Sea to the Gulf of Pelusium.

paths.title: Mediterranean in forty-eight hours
paths.notes: The book estimates about 600 leagues through the Mediterranean in forty-eight hours.

paths.title: Gibraltar to Vigo Bay
paths.notes: After the failed escape plan near Portugal, Nemo brings the Nautilus to the treasure wrecks in Vigo Bay.

paths.title: Vigo Bay to Atlantis
paths.notes: The Nautilus runs south to the Atlantic coordinate where Nemo reveals the vanished continent.

paths.title: Atlantis to submarine coal mines
paths.notes: Nemo enters a fictional volcanic lagoon where the Nautilus takes sodium for its electricity.

paths.title: Volcanic refuge to Sargasso Sea
paths.notes: The Nautilus reaches the weed-filled central Atlantic described as the Sargasso Sea.

paths.title: Dive to the Atlantic abyss
paths.notes: The book says that by 13 March the Nautilus had traveled about 13,000 leagues since the Pacific departure, then descends to 16,000 yards.

paths.title: Abyss to southern whale waters
paths.notes: The Nautilus resumes its southerly course and encounters whales and cachalots in southern latitudes.

paths.title: Southern Ocean to the South Pole
paths.notes: The Nautilus passes icebergs, dives beneath the ice, and reaches Nemo's fictional open sea at the South Pole.

paths.title: Ice tunnel imprisonment
paths.notes: After the pole, an overturned iceberg traps the Nautilus under ice until the crew cuts an escape.

paths.title: From Cape Horn to the Amazon
paths.notes: The Nautilus heads north, sights South America, passes the Plata, and rises near the Amazon mouth.

paths.title: Amazon to the poulps
paths.notes: The Nautilus passes the Guianas and Antilles before the giant-poulp attack.

paths.title: Gulf Stream to Long Island
paths.notes: The Nautilus follows the Gulf Stream past Hatteras toward Long Island during a storm.

paths.title: Atlantic cable to the Avenger
paths.notes: The Nautilus inspects the transatlantic cable, then reaches the Avenger wreck at 47 deg 24 min latitude, 17 deg 28 min longitude.

sourceRefs.label: latitude 47 deg 24 min and longitude 17 deg 28 min

paths.title: North Atlantic vengeance run
paths.notes: After sinking the warship, the Nautilus races north until it is drawn into the Lofoten Maelstrom near the end of the 20,000-league tour.

paths.title: Escape from the Maelstrom
paths.notes: The prisoners detach the dinghy and survive the Maelstrom, waking on the Lofoten coast.

chapterFacts.anchor: Atlantic reports of a shifting reef
locationFacts: The chapter surveys global reports of an unknown marine hazard.
No named route by the main characters has started.
deltaFacts: No mapped displacement.
slopeFacts: No travel slope.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: Introductory reports are not modeled as a route segment.

locationFacts: Aronnax is in New York after returning from Nebraska.
He is consulted about the sea monster before the naval expedition forms.
deltaFacts: No route segment starts until Aronnax accepts the invitation.
slopeFacts: Stationary surface chapter.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: New York is the narrative anchor but no displacement is assigned.

chapterFacts.anchor: New York to the Abraham Lincoln
locationFacts: Aronnax accepts the invitation aboard the Abraham Lincoln.
The frigate leaves Brooklyn pier.
deltaFacts: The mapped expedition begins with a short city transfer and the frigate's outbound voyage.
slopeFacts: Surface and sea-level travel.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: XYZ delta uses New York/Brooklyn waypoints and the first part of the frigate route.

locationFacts: Ned Land is introduced aboard the frigate.
The expedition continues outward toward the Pacific search zone.
deltaFacts: No new waypoint is introduced; the frigate route continues.
slopeFacts: Sea-level frigate route.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The chapter is represented by the Abraham Lincoln search path.

locationFacts: The Abraham Lincoln crosses the tropic of Capricorn at 105 degrees longitude.
The frigate crosses the equator on the 110th meridian, then searches the North Pacific near Japan.
The monster is sighted at 31 deg 15 min N, 136 deg 42 min E.
deltaFacts: The route reaches the explicit Japan encounter coordinate.
slopeFacts: Surface sea route.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: XYZ delta uses the text's Pacific coordinates and Cape Horn shaping.

locationFacts: The Abraham Lincoln pursues the luminous object at speed.
The chase remains in the waters near the Japan coordinate.
deltaFacts: The map keeps this chapter on the same encounter segment.
slopeFacts: Surface chase; no depth modeled yet.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The chase is localized near the Japan encounter waypoint.

locationFacts: The frigate collides with the unknown vessel.
Aronnax, Conseil, and Ned Land are thrown into the sea and reach the Nautilus.
deltaFacts: The route changes from frigate to swim/drift and boarding.
slopeFacts: Surface to shallow submerged boarding point.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The short castaway segment shares the Japan encounter coordinate but adds shallow depth.

locationFacts: The prisoners discover the interior of the Nautilus.
The route is now locked to Nemo's submarine.
deltaFacts: No long-distance movement is assigned beyond boarding.
slopeFacts: Shallow submerged state.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The boarding waypoint is retained as the active location.

locationFacts: Ned Land's frustration with captivity is foregrounded.
The submarine route has not yet been formally plotted by Nemo.
deltaFacts: No new path starts in this chapter.
slopeFacts: No additional vertical change.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The scene remains aboard the Nautilus near the initial boarding area.

locationFacts: Captain Nemo names the Nautilus and declares his severance from land.
The chapter is primarily explanatory and internal to the vessel.
deltaFacts: No mapped displacement.
slopeFacts: No new depth movement.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: No path starts; the chapter explains the vessel and its commander.

locationFacts: Nemo explains the electric systems and instruments of the Nautilus.
The chapter stays aboard the vessel.
deltaFacts: No new geographic displacement.
slopeFacts: No route slope.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: Technical interior chapter; no segment is assigned.

locationFacts: Nemo gives dimensions and operating principles for the Nautilus.
The text explains how the submarine rises, sinks, and moves horizontally.
deltaFacts: No new route path starts here.
slopeFacts: The chapter explains vertical movement but does not map a journey leg.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: No route delta; this chapter informs later depth modeling.

locationFacts: Nemo fixes the starting point and takes the Nautilus into the Japanese current.
The vessel runs about fifty yards below the sea.
deltaFacts: The true submarine route begins from the Japan boarding point.
slopeFacts: Shallow underwater travel at roughly fifty yards below the surface.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: XYZ delta starts the Japan-to-Crespo submarine leg.

locationFacts: Nemo invites the prisoners to a submarine hunt near Crespo Island.
The text gives Crespo's coordinate and its distance from the starting point.
deltaFacts: The route reaches the Crespo coordinate in the North Pacific.
slopeFacts: Shallow submarine transit, about twenty-five to thirty fathoms in this period.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The segment uses the book's 1,800-mile distance to Crespo.

locationFacts: The party leaves the Nautilus in diving suits.
The Nautilus is stranded in five fathoms for the walk.
deltaFacts: The path changes from submarine travel to a short sea-floor excursion.
slopeFacts: Descent to roughly nine meters below sea level.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The route uses the Crespo coordinate with a shallow depth offset.

locationFacts: The walkers cross the undersea forest and return by the Nautilus light.
The terrain includes slopes and a cliff-like island base.
deltaFacts: The short undersea loop ends back at the Nautilus.
slopeFacts: The model keeps this as a shallow diving path rather than a long horizontal run.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The route is localized at Crespo with a shallow sea-floor depth.

locationFacts: The Nautilus continues its long under-Pacific passage.
Aronnax traces the route on the chart while the submarine keeps southeast.
deltaFacts: The route leaves Crespo for the South Pacific island chain.
slopeFacts: Underwater route at ordinary cruising depths.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The distance is constrained toward the four-thousand-league Pacific arc.

sourceRefs.label: four thousand leagues under the Pacific

locationFacts: The Nautilus passes Pomotou/Tuamotu, Tahiti, and New Hebrides waters.
Nemo brings the submarine to Vanikoro and the La Perouse wreck site.
deltaFacts: The Pacific arc reaches Vanikoro.
slopeFacts: Mostly shallow submarine travel; Vanikoro reef waters are tens of fathoms deep.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: XYZ delta uses explicit Vanou harbor coordinates and South Pacific shaping points.

locationFacts: The Nautilus leaves Vanikoro for Papua and Torres Strait.
It grounds on a reef while trying to pass through the strait.
deltaFacts: The book gives 750 leagues from Vanikoro to the southeast point of Papua.
slopeFacts: The route rises into shallow reef water at the grounding.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: XYZ delta uses a book-distance leg from Vanikoro to an estimated Torres reef point.

locationFacts: The prisoners go ashore while waiting for the tide to free the Nautilus.
The chapter includes hunting and gathering on land.
deltaFacts: A short boat landing branches away from the grounded submarine.
A short inland foot segment represents the hunting and gathering excursion.
slopeFacts: Sea-level boat route and land movement.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The landing point is estimated near the Torres reef grounding.

locationFacts: The landing party returns as islanders approach the Nautilus.
Nemo's electric defense prevents boarding.
deltaFacts: The short boat branch returns to the grounded submarine.
slopeFacts: Surface route.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The same Gueboroar landing segment represents the return branch.

locationFacts: The strange sleep episode follows the Torres Strait crisis.
The route resumes only after the coral kingdom chapter.
deltaFacts: No new mapped segment starts here.
slopeFacts: No route slope.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The chapter remains aboard the Nautilus without a distinct waypoint.

locationFacts: The Nautilus visits the coral cemetery after leaving the Torres region.
The route then heads into the Indian Ocean.
deltaFacts: The Indian Ocean crossing begins after the coral kingdom.
slopeFacts: Submarine route at moderate depth.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The chapter starts the Torres-to-Ceylon route.

locationFacts: The Nautilus cruises through the Indian Ocean.
It passes near Cocos and observes Indian Ocean marine life.
deltaFacts: The route advances west across the Indian Ocean.
slopeFacts: The text says the Nautilus usually floats between fifty and one hundred fathoms deep.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: XYZ delta uses Torres, open Indian Ocean, Cocos, and Ceylon shaping.

locationFacts: Nemo proposes a visit to Ceylon's pearl fisheries.
The submarine nears the island.
deltaFacts: The Indian Ocean crossing approaches the pearl-bank endpoint.
slopeFacts: Shallowing route toward Ceylon.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The chapter remains on the Torres-to-Ceylon segment.

locationFacts: Nemo takes the party to the pearl bank west of Ceylon.
A shark attack interrupts the dive, and Nemo gives the rescued diver pearls.
deltaFacts: The Indian Ocean leg reaches Ceylon and adds a short diving excursion.
slopeFacts: Shallow sea-floor walk at the pearl bank.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: XYZ delta combines the end of the Indian Ocean route with the localized pearl dive.

locationFacts: The Nautilus leaves Ceylon, passes Aden, and enters the Red Sea.
Ned Land doubts that this route can lead back to Europe.
deltaFacts: The route moves northwest from Ceylon to the Red Sea.
slopeFacts: Submarine travel at ordinary cruising depths.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: XYZ delta uses Ceylon, Aden, and the Red Sea latitude anchor.

locationFacts: Nemo explains the fictional tunnel beneath Suez.
The Nautilus passes from the Red Sea to the Mediterranean in minutes.
deltaFacts: A hidden undersea tunnel replaces any surface Suez Canal route.
slopeFacts: Submarine tunnel route, shallow compared with ocean abyss segments.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: XYZ delta uses Red Sea and Pelusium endpoints with a Suez mouth control point.

locationFacts: The Nautilus crosses eastern Mediterranean waters near Crete and the Greek islands.
Nemo secretly aids a Cretan diver.
deltaFacts: The Mediterranean crossing begins from Pelusium.
slopeFacts: Submarine route with deeper Aegean water.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: XYZ delta uses Pelusium, Crete, and Greek Archipelago shaping points.

locationFacts: The Nautilus crosses the Mediterranean in forty-eight hours.
The text estimates this Mediterranean course at about 600 leagues.
deltaFacts: The route exits the Mediterranean through Gibraltar.
slopeFacts: Deep Mediterranean basin route, then a shallow strait.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: XYZ delta is constrained by the book's 600-league Mediterranean distance.

locationFacts: Ned Land plans an escape near Europe, but the Nautilus dives.
Nemo brings the prisoners to the treasure wrecks in Vigo Bay.
deltaFacts: The route runs from Gibraltar to Vigo Bay.
slopeFacts: Mostly shallow submarine coastal route.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: XYZ delta uses Gibraltar and Vigo Bay geocoding.

locationFacts: Nemo leads Aronnax on a night walk across the ruins of Atlantis.
The text gives the Nautilus coordinate as 33 deg 22 min latitude and 16 deg 17 min longitude.
deltaFacts: The route leaves Vigo for the Atlantic Atlantis coordinate.
slopeFacts: Submerged walk at moderate depth in the Atlantic.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: Longitude is modeled west because the scene lies in the Atlantic, 150 leagues from the nearest coast.

locationFacts: The Nautilus enters a hidden volcanic lagoon.
Nemo gathers sodium-bearing coal for the submarine's electricity.
deltaFacts: The route enters a fictional volcanic refuge.
slopeFacts: The route rises from submerged Atlantic travel into a shallow enclosed lagoon.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The lagoon is fictional and placed west of Atlantis as an Atlantic shaping point.

locationFacts: The Nautilus crosses the Sargasso Sea.
By 13 March it has made about 13,000 leagues since the Pacific departure.
It dives to 16,000 yards in the Atlantic abyss.
deltaFacts: The route runs from the volcanic refuge through Sargasso and down into the abyss.
slopeFacts: Major descent to the deepest modeled point in this book.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: XYZ delta combines Sargasso travel with the book's 16,000-yard depth.

locationFacts: The Nautilus resumes southward travel.
Nemo attacks cachalots to defend whales.
deltaFacts: The route leaves the abyss for southern latitudes.
slopeFacts: Ascent from abyss to ordinary submarine depth, then surface-near action.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The chapter starts from the abyss waypoint and returns to southern ocean cruising depth.

locationFacts: The Nautilus enters Antarctic ice fields.
Nemo prepares to pass beneath the ice toward the pole.
deltaFacts: The route continues south through the Southern Ocean.
slopeFacts: Submarine route under ice, with deeper submerged travel than open-water cruising.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The route uses Antarctic ice-edge shaping before the pole.

locationFacts: Nemo reaches a fictional open sea at the South Pole.
He lands, observes the sun, and claims the pole.
deltaFacts: The route reaches its southernmost point.
slopeFacts: Ascent from under-ice travel to near-surface polar water.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The South Pole waypoint is fictional and marks Nemo's claimed endpoint.

locationFacts: An overturned iceberg imprisons the Nautilus under the ice.
The submarine lies in an ice tunnel with air running down.
deltaFacts: The route departs the pole and becomes trapped beneath the ice.
slopeFacts: Descent to a trapped under-ice depth.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The ice-prison position is inferred north of the pole with a depth near the text's hundreds-of-yards range.

locationFacts: The crew cuts ice below the Nautilus while air runs out.
The submarine finally breaks free.
deltaFacts: The same under-ice segment ends with escape from the trap.
slopeFacts: Modeled as trapped depth with an eventual ascent.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The chapter uses the ice-prison segment with depth noted in the waypoint.

locationFacts: The Nautilus heads north, sights South America, passes the Plata, and reaches the Amazon mouth.
Aronnax notes 1,600 miles since the polar escape in this section.
deltaFacts: The route turns from Antarctic waters to equatorial South America.
slopeFacts: Ascent from under-ice conditions to ordinary coastal submarine cruising.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: XYZ delta uses Cape Horn, Plata, Guianas, and Amazon control points.

locationFacts: The Nautilus passes the Guianas and Antilles.
Giant poulps attack the submarine and one crewman is lost.
deltaFacts: The route moves north from the Amazon into the Antilles/North Atlantic.
slopeFacts: Near-surface action when the crew fights on the platform.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The battle coordinate is estimated from the described Antilles/North Atlantic progression.

locationFacts: The Nautilus follows the Gulf Stream past Hatteras.
It nears Long Island during heavy weather, frustrating escape.
deltaFacts: The route reaches waters near New York again.
slopeFacts: Near-surface storm route with intermittent diving.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: XYZ delta uses Hatteras/Gulf Stream and Long Island waypoints.

locationFacts: The Nautilus follows the transatlantic cable.
It reaches the wreck of the Avenger at the chapter's latitude/longitude.
deltaFacts: The route leaves Long Island for the eastern Atlantic.
slopeFacts: Deep descent to cable and wreck depths.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: XYZ delta uses cable shaping and the book's Avenger coordinate.

sourceRefs.label: latitude 47 deg 24 min to longitude 17 deg 28 min

locationFacts: A warship attacks the Nautilus.
Nemo uses the submarine's spur to sink it.
deltaFacts: The north Atlantic vengeance run begins after the Avenger coordinate.
slopeFacts: Near-surface attack followed by submerged ramming.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The path continues from the Avenger coordinate toward the far north.

locationFacts: The Nautilus races north after the sinking.
Nemo becomes increasingly isolated and grief-stricken.
deltaFacts: The route continues toward Norway.
slopeFacts: Alternating surface and underwater travel.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: The northbound segment uses an estimated North Atlantic control point.

locationFacts: The Nautilus is drawn into the Lofoten Maelstrom.
Aronnax, Conseil, and Ned Land escape in the dinghy and recover on the Norwegian coast.
Aronnax reports crossing 20,000 leagues in more than ten months.
deltaFacts: The submarine tour closes at the Maelstrom and the survivors reach shore.
slopeFacts: Violent surface whirlpool route after a long submarine run.
chapterFacts.xyzEstimate: XYZ delta ends at the Lofoten Maelstrom, with a short escape segment to shore.
